common_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: a production building turnaround contact sheet for Sin Star I, Neris planet, intended as visual reference for 3D reconstruction. Produce one high-resolution square 2-by-2 grid, exactly FOUR panels showing ONE identical building from four cardinal sides. Upper left FRONT, upper right BACK, lower left LEFT, lower right RIGHT. True straight-on orthographic elevation views at identical scale, no perspective convergence, no three-quarter angles, no isometric views. All structure and roof visible in every cell, comfortably framed with generous white margins; consistent ground baseline and consistent building dimensions, matching roof shape, doors, windows and attached details across all views. Use a plain very pale warm-gray studio background, subtle contact shadow only, no terrain base, horizon, setting, people, animals, vehicles, vegetation, floating props or surrounding architecture. Thin understated gray grid gutters. Small clear label FRONT / BACK / LEFT / RIGHT beneath its corresponding view, outside the object silhouette, no other text on the sheet unless a title is requested. Fully colored high-quality realistic stylized JRPG game-asset render, crisp physically plausible geometry and materials rather than a pencil drawing or blueprint. Neris architectural family derived from existing Sin Star artwork: warm ivory limestone, deep navy/cobalt blue roof tiles and trim, restrained aged gold/brass edges, pointed arched openings, subtle eight-point star motifs, occasional small inset cyan relay crystals. Lived-in but well-maintained, appealing and dignified science-fantasy civilization. Readable large forms, moderate decorative detail, solid buildable architecture, closed doors and windows, no interior cutaway. Ground-floor doors must feel human scale. Do not use text labels/signage as the primary building identity; use simple sculpted shop emblems where relevant. The aim is a clean consistent modeling reference, not a scene illustration.

buildings.name: Weapon Shop
buildings.spec: Design a compact two-storey WEAPON SHOP. Rectangular footprint approximately 10 m wide by 8 m deep, 9 m total height, main navy gabled roof with ridge front to rear. Warm ivory stone walls, brass joint straps and a restrained gold roof crest. Front: centered pointed arch double door, one large shuttered display window on each side, a clearly modeled crossed-swords emblem in a stone roundel above the door, three small upper arched windows. Back: solid stone workshop wall, centered closed loading double-door and two small upper windows; a substantial rectangular forge chimney integrated into the building's rear-left corner, never detached. Left flank: three workshop windows at ground level and three small upstairs windows, chimney at the rear end. Right flank: a closed side service door plus two windows below and three windows above. Keep the chimney attached at that SAME physical rear-left corner as the views rotate. A low two-step stone entrance belongs only to the front. Blackened bronze forge ventilation and slightly worn edges distinguish the trade. No loose weapons outside, no smoke, no flames. Exactly four consistent views of this single weapon shop.

buildings.name: Armor Shop
buildings.spec: Design a sturdy ARMOR SHOP, distinct from the weapon shop. Broad squat two-storey footprint approximately 12 m wide by 9 m deep, 8 m total height. Heavy ivory limestone wall piers and chamfered square corner buttresses support a broad low navy hipped roof with restrained brass seams. An armored, protective architectural silhouette. Front: central recessed double door under a pointed arch; one wide closed shuttered display opening on each side; a simple relief of a breastplate on a shield directly over the doorway; a row of three small upper windows. Back: a closed broad loading door centered below three upper windows, small workshop vent at ground floor on each side. Both side elevations: three repeated stone bays with matching small upper windows; left side has a closed service door in the middle ground bay, right side has a shuttered workshop window there instead. Shallow two-step front stoop. Small gold eight-point star roundels on corner piers. No freestanding armor, mannequin, rack, weapon, smoke or banners obscuring the walls. Exactly four consistent views of this single armor shop.

buildings.name: Items Shop
buildings.spec: Design an ITEMS AND SUPPLIES SHOP, a welcoming apothecary/general-store landmark distinct from the heavier combat shops. Compact two-storey square footprint approximately 8 m by 8 m, 9 m height. Ivory limestone lower storey and warm cream plaster upper storey framed by narrow brass trim, steep navy pyramidal tiled roof and a small solid octagonal roof lantern centered on top. Front: an arched double entrance in the center, matching broad closed arched display windows either side, fixed short navy awnings attached above the two windows; carved potion-flask emblem above the entrance, no written shop name. Upper level: two small arched windows. Back: one plain closed service door with a small high window on each side, two upper windows. Left and right sides each have two ground-floor arched windows and two upper windows; shallow inset wall cupboards visible as closed shutters below windows. Two tiny cyan crystal wall lamps flank the front door, all other decoration restrained. Clean inviting well-used shop; no loose bottles, crates, street stall, climbing vines or outdoor inventory. Exactly four consistent views of this single items shop.

buildings.name: Communication Tower
buildings.spec: Design a Neris COMMUNICATION TOWER: a tall distinctive working science-fantasy civic relay, approximately 24 m tall on a 7 m square base. A solid tapered four-sided ivory stone tower with chamfered corners and slim navy inset vertical panels, brass structural bands and a small cyan relay crystal under a protective gold-edged lantern at the summit. The summit has four identical integrated short brass fin antennas pointing in cardinal directions, and a solid pointed navy metal cap. The mast and fin supports connect physically to the tower; no floating rings or levitating pieces. FRONT base has a tall closed pointed-arch maintenance double door with a small eight-point star relief above; BACK base has two closed rectangular equipment shutters and a vent; LEFT and RIGHT base each have a single tall narrow closed window. Midshaft has three vertically stacked slim dark windows on each face, and small inset cyan signal strips, subtle enough not to obscure material. Human-scaled base door makes the tower's height legible. Restrained elegance consistent with Neris's blue-roofed stone city, not a generic modern telecom mast, not a cathedral. No cables to offscreen anchors, no satellite dishes beyond frame, no glow halos, electricity arcs, giant foundation terrain or pedestal. Exactly four consistent cardinal elevations of this ONE communication tower.

buildings.name: Town Hall / City Center
buildings.spec: Design the Neris TOWN HALL / CITY CENTER as the largest civic building in this asset set. Monumental three-storey ivory stone hall, approximate footprint 34 m wide by 22 m deep, main dome peak 24 m high, clearly many times the mass of a small shop. Strong symmetrical civic architecture: a central square hall crowned by a cobalt-blue eight-sided dome with thin gold ribs and a small gold eight-point star finial; two broad lower two-storey navy-roofed wings attached on either side. Front: central elevated entrance portico of four substantial stone piers framing three pointed arches and a closed main double door, broad shallow integrated stone steps, repeated arched windows in each lateral wing, a large eight-point star medallion above the portico. Back: same main hall and attached wings, a modest closed central service entry reached by two steps, regular arched windows, no front portico duplicated on rear. Left and right: consistent depth, repeated stone bays and windows, clearly attached wing roof below the central dome. Dome physically supported by solid drum; simple buttresses, restrained gold cornices, small inset cyan civic-relay details. No clock, religious cross, giant statues, political logos, flags obscuring architecture, freestanding fountains, courtyard wall or surrounding city. Emphasize substantial large spaces with human-scale doors and many regular window bays. Exactly four consistent views of the same grand civic building.

buildings.name: Home 1 — Modest Cottage
buildings.spec: Design RESIDENTIAL HOME 1, a modest comfortable Neris cottage for an ordinary household. One storey plus an attic, footprint approximately 7 m wide by 6 m deep, roof peak 6 m. Simple rectangular ivory limestone-and-cream-plaster structure, steep navy gabled tile roof with ridge front to back and a small centered stone chimney at the rear ridge. Front: an offset wooden arched door on the viewer's left, a broad closed two-part shuttered window on the right, a single small attic window centered high in the front gable; a shallow two-step entrance stoop. Back: one closed plain service door centered and two small ground-floor windows, a small centered attic vent. Left and right sides: each two small closed arched windows; no secondary gables. Slim blue shutters, modest brass hinges, a small eight-point-star stone door keystone. It should feel humble, warm and unmistakably residential, not a shop, fort or palace. No merchant emblem, open shopfront, awnings, hanging laundry, fence, plants, garden, furniture or freestanding props. All view geometry corresponds to the same cottage, chimney remains at the same rear location.

buildings.name: Home 2 — Family House
buildings.spec: Design RESIDENTIAL HOME 2, a roomy two-storey Neris family house distinct from the modest cottage. Rectangular footprint approximately 11 m wide by 8 m deep and 9 m high. Broad navy hipped tile roof above warm ivory limestone lower storey and cream plaster upper storey, solid square corners, restrained gold/brass edging. Front: central closed arched wooden door, two large closed shuttered windows on the ground floor, three upper windows, the center upper window opens onto a small shallow stone balcony with thick solid balustrade supported directly by the entrance portico below. Back: centered closed service door, two downstairs windows and three upstairs windows, no balcony. Left and right elevations each have two downstairs and two upstairs windows; one small rear roof chimney consistently placed. Only shallow front entry steps, no raised landscape platform. Blue shutters and a modest eight-point-star keystone over the front door. Comfortable human proportions and practical lived-in material wear. No shop signs, loose domestic props, vegetation, people, clotheslines, swimming pool, fence or surrounding houses. Exactly four corresponding views of this one house.

buildings.name: Home 3 — Roundhouse
buildings.spec: Design RESIDENTIAL HOME 3, a distinctive cozy octagonal two-storey Neris roundhouse. Single solid regular octagonal footprint approximately 8 m across, 10 m tall with a steep eight-faceted navy tiled pavilion roof meeting at one brass-capped point, NOT a dome, plus small integrated chimney near the back of the roof. Warm ivory stone ground floor, cream plaster upper floor with narrow stone ribs on eight corners and restrained aged-brass trim. FRONT main facet has a closed arched wooden entry door at ground level and a single narrow upper window, flanking diagonal facets each have a ground and upper window. BACK main facet has a small closed maintenance hatch low and a narrow upper window, flanking facets continue same pattern. LEFT and RIGHT main facets each have one large closed shuttered window on ground floor and one narrow upper window, adjacent angled faces appear as narrow foreshortened facets in straight cardinal elevations. Two shallow front entry steps only. Blue shutters, small star-relief door keystone, no turret attached, no exterior staircase, no balcony, no garden, props or people. Clearly a modest HOUSE and distinct silhouette from rectangular homes, no commercial signage or civic antenna. Exactly four consistent views of one octagonal home.
